text.p: Kinross Gold Corp plans to use the proceeds from its C$200 million convertible debenture issue to fund acquisitions and expand its existing operations, company chairman Bob Buchan said Thursday.
"This gives us the credibility to move into the global field," Buchan told Reuters in a phone interview.

Earlier Thursday, Kinross announced a bought deal for C$200 million in convertible debentures bearing 5.5 percent and maturing December 5, 2006. They are convertible into common shares of Kinross Gold at C$13.35 per share.
"We now have close to C$290 million on hand," Buchan said.
"That gives us the credibility to look for investment opportunities anywhere on the planet."
The company's demands for capital are growing as it moves to expand and explore at its Hoyle Pond property in the Timmins area of Northern Ontario and at its Nevada interests, Buchan said.

Kinross aims to be producing one million ounces of gold a year by 1998, he said. Right now, the company produces at about half that rate, but current projects will bring production up to about 800,000 by 1998, leaving 200,000 ounces to come through acquistions, he said.
"We've grown by acquisition. I'm very comfortable with that method of growth," Buchan said, adding he prefers late-stage development gold projects or projects already in production.

Kinross's issue is the second announcement of convertible debentures on the Toronto market this week. Sherritt International Corp raised C$675 million through convertible debentures this week in an oversubscribed issue.
"We were reacting to the market," said Buchan. He said the company sped up its issue when it saw how successful Sherritt's was.
"That's the fashion these days," said mining analyst Tony Hayes at brokerage Credifinance. "People are chasing yield."
